rationale: Build on the current Bigram64 winner by keeping its exact main branch and adding one small rank-16 corrective bigram branch. The extra branch stays below the float-keep threshold as separate tensors, so this spends the remaining artifact budget on more n-gram capacity without forcing the whole tail into the worse quantized-rank80 regime. Training dynamics, quant-aware endgame, eval, and compile-stable shapes stay otherwise unchanged.
title: Two-Branch Float-Kept Bigram Tail On Bigram64 Best
